co_allied_wall.blurb: Allied Wall is a recently developed sector inside Castlewood Canyon State Park, in the conglomerate canyon south of Denver. It holds a mix of sport lines, trad lines and a few top-rope setups, so you can bring a rack or just a rope and draws. Most climbs fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with one 5.12 and a couple of much easier options, so it suits climbers who are past the beginner stage. Several of the trad lines are noticeably taller than the usual lines in the park. Expect a busy canyon on fair-weather weekends.

co_dump_wall.blurb: Dump Wall is a small sport crag beside the highway near Twin Lakes, on the Independence Pass road. All thirteen routes are bolted, and they sit on both sides of the approach path. The difficulty runs from the low 5.10s up through 5.12 with one 5.13, so this is a spot for intermediate and stronger climbers rather than first-timers. The wall faces southeast and slips into shade around midday in summer, which makes it a handy morning stop; on bright winter days it can also be pleasant. Traffic on the road is fast, so take care pulling out.

co_duck_rock.blurb: Duck Rock is a small crag in the Badger Flats district of South Park, roughly an hour west of Colorado Springs at around 9,500 feet. Thirteen routes, mostly bolted single pitches with two trad lines, run from very easy up to about 5.9, which makes it one of the friendlier places in the district for newer leaders. The granite faces south and has shady trees at the staging spots, so it warms up well in cooler weather. Summer and fall are the usual seasons across Badger Flats, with winter days possible when the sun is out.

co_hot_spot_area.blurb: Hot Spot Area is one lettered section along the cliff band of North Table Mountain near Golden, set between Winterfest Wall and Winter Warmer Area. Climbs here are a roughly even mix of sport and trad, from easy fives up to a couple of 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The band as a whole faces south and west, so it stays comfortable in cold weather, but the rock has polished in places and the tops can be loose. Routes tend to be short, and rattlesnakes are around in summer and fall.

co_little_half_dome.blurb: Little Half Dome is a quiet granite dome in the Deckers climbing district southwest of Denver, past Atlantis. The thirteen climbs are mostly bolted with a handful of trad lines, ranging from easy fifth class to the low 5.11s and concentrated around 5.9. Friction is the main technique and the rock quality is uneven, so favor the friction and be wary of questionable holds. Fresh bolts have gone in recently, and visitors rarely meet crowds here. Allow extra time to locate lines, since the neighborhood's route information is changeable.

co_notchtop.blurb: Notchtop is a big alpine formation in Rocky Mountain National Park, reached from the Bear Lake trailhead. Nearly all of its climbs are multi-pitch alpine trad, from moderate classics around 5.4 and 5.7 up to a handful of hard 5.11 and 5.12 testpieces, with the steep, exposed crack climbing of the south side the best known. The approach is a long hike of just over three miles and well over a thousand feet of gain. Descent is by a fourth-class ridge or several double-rope rappels. It can be climbed across much of the year, including in winter.
